fight: Is the box's PCIe fabric Gen2 x4 (the repo's premise) or Gen2 x16 (achievable with the capacitor mod)?

side_a.position: Gen2 x4 — the stock, community-normal configuration. Width is set by the slot and by 12 of 16 lanes being depopulated.
claims: Stock electrical link is Gen1 x4 (~1 GB/s); the software Gen unlock lifts speed to Gen2 but width stays whatever the caps allow
Stock card has missing AC-coupling capacitors on 12 of 16 lanes, so width beyond x4 is physically blocked
All CMP 170HX report x4 (downgraded) from an x16 capability; x4 is normal, x2 is not

side_b.position: Gen2 x16 is achievable and measured — the capacitor mod restores the lanes, and a 4-card PLX host trains all cards at Gen2 x16.
claims: With the cmpunlocker link patch all four cards on the 4-card PLX host train Gen2 x16; Gen3 is blocked by the OPT_DISABLE_GEN3_SPEED fuse
Width beyond x4 needs 24 x 0402 220 nF X7R capacitors soldered on; a four-card Gen2 x16 field report shows zero PCIe errors at 5.97 GB/s
Measured BF16 164.4-192.7 TFLOPS against a 202.1 ceiling, and 6.63-6.67 GB/s single-card PCIe bandwidth

evidence_quality_delta: Side B has measured field reports on real 170HX boxes; side A has spec sheets plus stock-configuration measurements. Side B is stronger where it applies.
scope_overlap: Both right, scoped differently: x4 is the stock/normal slot; x16 requires a hardware mod. The repo assumes the pessimistic default without stating the mod exists.

fight: Is peer-to-peer actually unavailable on this box, or is 'no P2P' a driver mask that a patch lifts — and does lifting it break collectives?

side_a.position: No P2P. Collectives stage through host RAM; the GA100 mailbox path is a genuine dead end.
claims: No peer access with the plain unlock; copies stage through host memory at 6.21-6.30 GB/s at 256 MiB
P2P fused off (GNS); D2D host-staged at 5.85 GB/s
0 of 56 directed pairs have peer access

side_b.position: P2P works over BAR1 P2P once patched — verified with real transfers, not cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer.
claims: P2P works over BAR1 P2P, measured 1.68 GB/s each way on PCIe Gen2 x4, full 4-GPU mesh (12/12 directed pairs), verified with real transfers
P2P re-enabled via three bayley patches plus ForceP2P=0x11; TP=2 prefill then runs 1.8-1.9x faster

side_c.position: The P2P patch is unusable for training: it hangs every NCCL collective because BAR1 is 64 MB and blocks the static-BAR1 check.
claims: The P2P patch reportedly hangs every NCCL collective (BAR1 64 MB blocks the static-BAR1 check), so applying it would break DDP

evidence_quality_delta: Both sides measured. Side C is a compatibility finding, not a contradiction of side B's bandwidth number.
scope_overlap: Genuine disagreement about the patched path, plus a third position that resolves it: P2P bandwidth exists but the patch breaks NCCL, so training still stages through host memory.

fight: Is the box's per-GPU bf16 throughput ~162 TFLOPS (repo) or ~42 TFLOPS (published measurements)?

side_a.position: ~162 TFLOPS bf16 per GPU, ~810 TFLOPS aggregate — measured on the user's unlocked cards.
claims: A healthy card measures 155.7 TFLOPS fp16 versus 39.3 under PWRBRK#
Measured BF16 164.4-192.7 TFLOPS against a 202.1 ceiling
A100 312 TFLOPS bf16 dense at 108 SM scales to ~202 TFLOPS at 70 SM and ~214 at 74 SM; 162 is ~80% of ceiling

side_b.position: ~42 TFLOPS fp16 with tensor cores disengaged; PyTorch reaches only 6.3 TFLOPS.
claims: FP16 ~42 TFLOPS but PyTorch only 6.3; tensor cores unusable on the stock card
FP16 performance approximately 42 TFLOPS, unthrottled, the primary path for AI inference
170th Street spec sheet lists 49.05 TFLOPS fp16

evidence_quality_delta: Side A is measured on unlocked cards; side B is measured on stock cards. Neither refutes the other — the unlock is load-bearing.
scope_overlap: Both right, scoped by unlock state. The repo's number is only valid if tensor cores are enabled after unlock, which no source explicitly confirms.

fight: Does FSDP/ZeRO-3 cost 1.5x or 2x DDP's communication?

side_a.position: 1.5x — FSDP moves 3-Psi bytes per step against DDP's 2-Psi.
claims: Full sharding has 1.5x communication overhead and volume over DDP if using a bandwidth-optimal ring algorithm
DP = 2-Psi, ZeRO-3 = 3-Psi = 1.5x

side_b.position: 2x — the repo's research.md section 2 states FSDP costs roughly twice DDP.
claims: FSDP costs ~2x DDP on this fabric

evidence_quality_delta: Side A is two independent primaries deriving the same ratio; side B is the repo's own arithmetic.
scope_overlap: Genuine error in the repo. Worse, research.md's overhead table compares FSDP at 7B trainable against DDP at 1B trainable, conflating parameter count with strategy.

fight: Is DDP the only viable training topology on this fabric, or is pipeline parallelism a real alternative?

side_a.position: DDP is the only viable topology; PP, TP and EP are out.
claims: The choice is DDP or FSDP, and DDP is ~2x cheaper on the link
Drop EP and TP from the training topology candidates

side_b.position: PP is viable and beats TP by a wide margin; PP's per-step traffic is O(activations), not O(parameters).
claims: PP beats TP 6.6x on prefill (5,321 vs 801 tok/s at 77k); TP runs 86 all-reduces per forward over a no-P2P link
PP+offload uses zero GPU P2P and beats ZeRO-2/FSDP/ZeRO-Inf/Megatron-PP/TP by 1.48-2.16x on 8x4090
Mobius: PCIe 3.0 16 GB/s vs 900 GB/s NVLink; ZeRO traffic 7.3x model size per step, >70% time; 3.8-5.1x via PP+cross-mapping
TP-free PP+ZeRO-3 (ZeroPP) is up to 33% faster than Megatron 3D parallelism

evidence_quality_delta: Side B has multiple measured results, but most are inference/serving; RoundPipe and Mobius are training measurements on consumer PCIe.
scope_overlap: Genuine fork. PP is viable for training, and the repo drops it without argument.

fight: Is expert parallelism ruled out by the fabric (~70x compute time), or merely degraded?

side_a.position: EP does two all-to-alls per MoE layer; at 1M-token batches that is ~70x the compute time. Ruled out.
claims: EP does two all-to-alls per MoE layer; at 1M-token batches that is ~70x the compute time on this fabric

side_b.position: EP is degraded but implementable; host-staged EP and head-parallel EP both work, and the optimized stacks are what is ruled out.
claims: No-P2P means every byte crosses PCIe twice; NCCL ring moves 2(N-1)S vs N*S (1.6x at N=5); ThunderEP gets 2.00x/1.53x dispatch/combine over NCCL
CoMoE: comms are 81.6% of MoE execution time on RTX 5090; host-as-routing-hub recovers 85-90% of A800+DeepEP at 23.4% cost
Head Parallel: O(1) comms regardless of k (25% of EP at k=4), 1.61x faster at 4B
DeepSeek-V3 cross-node EP gives an inefficient compute-to-communication ratio of approximately 1:1 on NVLink(160 GB/s)+IB(50 GB/s)

evidence_quality_delta: Side B has measured numbers; side A's 70x is arithmetic from stated assumptions and is reproduced by no source.
scope_overlap: The direction holds (EP is expensive), the magnitude does not. 'Ruled out' is a software-stack statement: every optimized EP stack requires NVLink/P2P/RDMA.

fight: Does CSA2 compressed sparse attention pay off at 32k training context?

side_a.position: Worth one experiment but the axis most likely to disappoint at 32k; the candidate cap barely binds at 32k.
claims: At 32k the indexer's candidate cap barely binds, so the sparse-attention win is smaller than the published 1M-context numbers suggest
CSA2 is the least-proven axis on this box

side_b.position: Sparse attention's value at 32k is granularity-dependent: token-granular selection is a net loss, block-granular is a large win.
claims: Measured 32K verdict: 0.83x total (1.08x fwd / 0.79x bwd) vs dense MLA; crossover 64K, 128K with packing
Blockwise NSA at 32k is 6.3x fwd / 3.4x bwd vs Triton FlashAttention-2
MoBA at 32K trailing loss 1.546 vs full attention 1.464; the 90/10 hybrid matches it
HISA: the 16,384 candidate cap does bind at 32k (2x)

side_c.position: The 32k blocker is the indexer score tensor's memory, not FLOPs — 64-128 GiB at 32k, fixed by chunked top-k but Hopper-only as shipped.
claims: Materialized [B,S,HI,T] FP32 indexer tensor is 64 GiB at S=32,768; 129 GB measured peak on a 140 GB H200; chunked partition-merge top-k cuts it to 0.40 GB
All DSA training kernels are SM90/SM100-only; CMP 170HX is GA100/SM80
ref_indexer_forward materialises (B,S_q,H_q,S_k) FP32 = 68.7 GB at 32k/H_q=16, over a 64 GB card

evidence_quality_delta: Side B and C are measured on H200/A100, not on this box. Side A is the repo's inference.
scope_overlap: The repo's verdict survives for CSA2 specifically, but its reasoning is wrong on two counts: the cap does bind at 32k, and the layer model (indexer on every layer) is wrong for 27 of 40 layers. V4.1 trains sparse attention at 64K, not 32k.

fight: Do frozen Engram memory tables make 7B-total / ~1B-trainable fit DDP on 64 GB cards, or is the frozen-table premise a misreading?

side_a.position: Frozen tables are pure VRAM: zero optimizer state, zero per-token FLOPs, the cheapest capacity available.
claims: Frozen params carry no gradients and no optimizer state, so 7B total with ~1B trainable fits DDP at ~28 GB/card
Memory Grafting builds tables from a frozen donor model's hidden states and reports gains at 0.92B scale

side_b.position: Canonical Engram and every production-scale memory model train their tables; the training path is model-parallel sharding plus all-to-all, not DDP.
claims: Engram-27B = 26.7B total / 3.8B activated / 5.7B Engram; tables are TRAINED via model-parallel sharding plus All-to-All
LongCat-Flash-Lite: 68.5B total, 31.4B n-gram params (46%) trained from scratch; production scale does not freeze memory
UltraMemV2: 120B sparse memory params, 2.5B activated, trained from scratch
OverEncoding: plain FSDP on large embedding tables gives 25% slowdown and OOM above m=5e6; fix is embedding-layer tensor parallelism

side_c.position: Frozen tables do exist, but the literature's tables are an order of magnitude larger than the repo's design, so results do not transfer.
claims: Delta N-gram: T0 never modified, forward-only writes into a sparse patch, zero optimizer state — but the table is 51.2B params (~102 GB BF16) and training used EP4/DP4 on 4xH200
The '<3% overhead' number is inference-only in every source that reports it

evidence_quality_delta: Side B has production-scale training evidence; side C has measured systems costs. Side A is the repo's arithmetic.
scope_overlap: Genuine: the repo's premise is half right (frozen tables exist and remove optimizer state) and half wrong (the load-bearing production path trains tables, and the frozen path's real tables are far larger).

fight: Does 7B fully trainable really need FSDP, or does a cheaper optimizer state fit it on 64 GB?

side_a.position: 7B fully trainable needs ~112 GB per card with Adam, so it does not fit DDP on 64 GB.
claims: 7B all trainable: 14 GB weights + 14 GB grads + 84 GB Adam = 112 GB; needs FSDP

side_b.position: 8-bit Adam or Adafactor plausibly fit 7B fully trainable in 64 GB without freezing tables.
claims: 8-bit Optimizers: state is 33-75% of training memory; Adam 8 B -> 2 B/param (1B model 8 GB -> 2 GB); 7B fully trainable 84 GB -> ~14 GB state, ~42 GB total before activations
Adafactor: O(n+m) state, ~4 B/param worst case (~28 GB for 7B), matches Adam on WMT14 Transformer
Measured 7B BF16+Adam = 87 GB state -> DDP OOMs on 80 GB

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is measured and primary-sourced; side A is the repo's arithmetic with a fixed optimizer choice.
scope_overlap: Genuine: the repo's verdict is optimizer-choice-dependent, not architectural. This is the strongest challenge to the whole frozen-table premise.

fight: Is a fixed 1M-token global batch safe from step 0, or does critical batch size bind early in training?

side_a.position: Large global batches are the right lever; DDP overhead falls as batch size grows.
claims: At 1M-token global batches DDP overhead is ~36%; at 2M, ~18%

side_b.position: CBS is near zero at init, so a fixed 1M batch from step 0 degrades loss; batch-size warmup is required.
claims: Measured CBS plateaus at ~4,096 docs x 4,096 tok = 16.8M tokens on OLMo 1B/7B, so 1M is ~17x below CBS late; but CBS is approximately 0 at init

Best accuracy at m=2-32, explicitly against thousand-scale batches

fight: Is a 5-rank DDP world size benign, or is 5 GPUs a pathological configuration?

side_a.position: NCCL handles arbitrary world sizes; 5 ranks is fine.
claims: NCCL natively supports arbitrary and odd world sizes; ring handles uneven divisions transparently

side_b.position: 5 GPUs triggers significant NUMA effects and should be avoided.
claims: The NUMA effects appear quite significant with 5 GPUs; one should avoid adopting 5 GPUs in their application setup

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is a peer-reviewed measurement; side A is a capability statement, not a performance claim.
scope_overlap: Both right: 5 works, but it is slower than 4 or 8 for reasons unrelated to the link width.

fight: Does bf16 gradient compression actually halve all-reduce traffic on this box?

side_a.position: bf16_compress_hook halves gradient bytes (4 -> 2 per element).
claims: bf16_compress_hook halves gradient bytes (4->2/elem), divides before collective to avoid FP16 overflow; experimental, requires NCCL > 2.9.6

side_b.position: BF16 training still all-reduces in 32-bit, so the hook's saving may be smaller than assumed; FP8 would give 63-65% but GA100 has no FP8.
claims: FP8 all-reduce gives 63-65% practical comm reduction; BF16 training still all-reduces in 32-bit; FP8 is H100-native
GA100/sm_80 has no FP8 tensor cores

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is measured on H100; side A is the hook's documented behaviour.
scope_overlap: Unresolved for this box: the hook's actual saving depends on whether NCCL's bf16 path is honoured on GA100, which no source measures.

fight: Is the measured 0.75 GiB/s all-reduce a misconfiguration, or is it structural to NCCL on this fabric?

side_a.position: 0.75 GiB/s is the measured effective collective bandwidth on the box.
claims: NCCL all-reduce across 5 GPUs is ~0.75 GiB/s

side_b.position: The ceiling is structural: ring is non-pipelined, LL caps at 25-50% of peak, LL128 is disabled on PCIe, tree degenerates to a chain intra-node.
claims: NCCL LL forces a host buffer, capping at 25-50% of peak; LL128 is disabled on PCIe; Ring AllReduce is 2k-1 non-pipelined steps; Tree degenerates to a chain intra-node
NCCL SHM all-reduce busbw at 256 MiB is 3.69 GB/s same-switch, 3.85 cross-switch, 4.24 on 3 cards; 8 KiB latency 120-145 us
Hierarchical multi-path allreduce beats NCCL 1.25-1.38x at >=8 MB

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is measured and mechanistic; side A is a single user measurement with no error bars.
scope_overlap: Not a contradiction: 0.75 GiB/s is plausible as an end-to-end training number, while 3.69-4.24 GB/s is a bare collective benchmark. The gap between them is the finding.
